consensus_summary: All ten stakeholders — across clinical, compliance, operational, financial, and advocacy perspectives — acknowledge the strength of the underlying clinical case: refractory hyperglycemia despite maximally tolerated medical therapy, active multi-system end-organ damage, documented severe hypoglycemia burden, and STAMPEDE-level evidence supporting RYGB as a metabolic intervention. No stakeholder recommends outright denial on clinical grounds, and the Appeals & Grievances Specialist explicitly notes that a denial grounded solely in the step-therapy gap would likely fail external review. However, there is near-universal agreement — spanning the Medical Director, Compliance Officer, Director of Utilization Management, Finance Director, Nephrology Consultant, Behavioral Health Liaison, Pharmacy Benefit Manager, and Cotiviti Director — that the authorization record contains multiple unresolved documentation gaps that prevent approval as submitted: specifically, the absence of a formally adjudicated Medical Director exception for the one-month supervised program shortfall, the pharmacologically inaccurate Tirzepatide exclusion rationale, the complete absence of nephrology clearance and a perioperative renal protection protocol for a patient at eGFR 54 with a confirmed declining trajectory, and the staleness of the March 2026 psychiatric evaluation relative to the patient's post-March hypoglycemic ED visit and the distinct post-bariatric hypoglycemia risk profile. No stakeholder changed their position after reassessment; every reassessment served to reinforce or sharpen original concerns, with several stakeholders adding the nephrology and behavioral health gaps to their pre-conditions after those reviewers surfaced them in round two.
key_tensions: The patient's adult son (Raymond) and the Appeals & Grievances Specialist argue that denying or indefinitely deferring on the supervised program gap is a Catch-22 — the ED hospitalization causing the missed session is itself a direct product of the condition the surgery is intended to treat, and an external reviewer will not uphold a denial on that basis — while the Compliance Officer, Director of Utilization Management, Finance Director, and Medical Director hold that approving without a formally documented Medical Director exception creates an undocumented policy precedent with audit exposure under URAC standards and applicable state utilization review statutes, regardless of how defensible the individual decision may be.

The Pharmacy Benefit Manager and Cotiviti Director identify the Tirzepatide exclusion rationale as a material documentation deficiency — conflating SGLT2 inhibitor non-response with GLP-1 pathway failure is pharmacologically inaccurate and will not survive external audit — while the provider team has not submitted any corrected or supplemental clinical note; the Medical Director concurs this is a pharmacologic error, whereas the Nephrology Consultant notes the more immediate concern is whether a Tirzepatide trial is actually safe to require in a patient with active severe hypoglycemia and eGFR 54, a question none of the other reviewers have formally addressed.

The Nephrology Consultant and Behavioral Health Liaison both rate at 2 and flag acute procedural and post-surgical risk dimensions — perioperative AKI risk at eGFR 54 without nephrology clearance, and the inadequacy of a five-month-old psychiatric evaluation that predates the patient's most clinically significant hypoglycemic events — that were entirely absent from the original submission and that multiple colleagues in round two acknowledged as additive, unresolved prerequisites rather than peripheral concerns.
recommendation_rationale: The weight of stakeholder input across all lenses points uniformly to conditional deferral rather than approval or denial: the clinical case is strong enough that outright denial is widely regarded as indefensible on appeal, but the authorization record as submitted contains at least four discrete, formally unresolved gaps — a Medical Director exception determination on the supervised program step-therapy shortfall, a pharmacologically defensible and patient-specific Tirzepatide exclusion note from Dr. Nair, a nephrology clearance with a documented perioperative renal protection protocol, and an updated psychiatric evaluation with a prospective post-surgical behavioral health monitoring plan — none of which have been supplied and none of which any stakeholder has identified a basis for waiving. Authorization should be deferred with a clear written notice to the requesting providers specifying each outstanding item, a defined response timeline consistent with the plan's non-urgent pre-service turnaround requirements, and confirmation from the UM coordinator that concurrent review has been flagged for the anticipated 2–3 day inpatient stay.
